text: Those who enter Paradise are in perpetual bliss.
Generosity for the sake of Allah is the worship of those who are close [to Allah].
flag_note: contains bracketed editorial insertions

text: Generosity without fear or hope of recompense is true generosity.
Give generously and you will be honoured.
The most generous of you is the one who will gain the most.
The most excellent of noble traits is generosity.
The best generosity is to forgive after gaining the upper hand.
The greatest generosity is being open-handed with whatever is available.
The greatest generosity is delivering the rights to their [rightful] owners.
The greatest generosity is giving despite [facing] hard times.
Generosity is [true] leadership, sovereignty is [only] administration.
Generosity is a present honour.
Generosity is the protector of honour.
The bane of generosity is poverty.
The bane of generosity is wastefulness.
Through generosity, authority is acquired.
Generosity stems from nobility of character.
Through generosity, men gain authority.
Through generosity, distinction is established and praise is acquired.
Be generous with whatever you have, [and] you will be praised.
Be generous and you will gain authority; be patient and you will be triumphant.
The generosity of the poor is the best generosity.
Be generous with what is available, fulfil your promises and be loyal with the trusts [that have been entrusted to you].
The generosity of a poor person dignifies him and the stinginess of a rich person debases him.
Be generous with that which perishes and you will be compensated for it with that which lasts.
Be generous for the sake of Allah and struggle against your selves in obedience to Him, He will [in return] magnify your reward and increase His favour upon you.
Generosity is the practice of the honourable.
The highest extent of generosity is giving [from] whatever is available.
One who is open-handed does good to others.
One who is generous gains authority.
One who does not show generosity is not praised.
How excellent is generosity when in straitened circumstances!
One who does not give generously while he is praised has to give away while he is dispraised.
One who does not give generously does not gain authority.
The generosity of a man endears him to his rivals and his stinginess makes him hated by his [own] children.
The generous person is loved and praised, even if nothing of his generosity reaches his praiser, and the stingy person is the opposite of this.
The one who is generous is praised in this world and felicitous in the Hereafter.
Verily the masters of the people of this world (and the Hereafter) are the generous.
Be generous with the truth and miserly with falsehood.
Be [either] selflessly generous or moderate in giving but do not be from the third kind (i.e. the misers).
One who is close to Allah is safe, while [one who is] His enemy is frightened.
Proximity to Allah is granted to those who obey Him and keep away from disobedience to Him.
The worst of neighbours is the wicked neighbour.
A wicked neighbour is the greatest adversity and the most serious tribulation.
Be a neighbour to one from whose evil you are safe and whose goodness does not turn away from you.
Ask about the neighbour before the house.
Being a bad neighbour and offending the virtuous are the worst forms of vileness.
One who is neighbourly gets many neighbours.
One who is good to his neighbours gets many helpers.
Taking care of one’s neighbour is an act of magnanimity.
Hunger is better than the humiliation of subjugation.
Keeping oneself hungry is the most beneficial cure, whereas eating to one’s fill increases maladies.
Hunger is better than subjugation.
Complement your food with hunger and discipline yourself with contentment.
The best condiment is hunger.
How good an assistant of piety hunger is!
How good an assistant in cutting down the [desires of the carnal] self and breaking its [bad] habits hunger is!
flag_note: contains bracketed editorial insertions

text: The alms-tax of high rank [and power] is benefitting others with it.
flag_note: contains bracketed editorial insertions

text: One of the obligations of a person who possesses a high rank is to use it to grant the [needs of] one who seeks from him.
flag_note: contains bracketed editorial insertions

text: One who benefits others with his high rank makes himself praiseworthy.
Whoever makes an effort to strive in obedience to Allah and His messenger, his soul shall be safe and sound [from the torments of the Hereafter] and his transaction will be profitable and gainful.
flag_note: contains bracketed editorial insertions

text: The first thing which you overcome through Jihād is through striving with your hands, then [if this is not possible] by your tongue, then [if this is not possible] with your hearts; and the one who neither supports good with his heart nor censures evil, is turned upside down (i.e. will face the wrath of Allah).
flag_note: contains bracketed editorial insertions

text: Struggling [in the way of Allah] is the pillar of faith and the path of the felicitous.
flag_note: contains bracketed editorial insertions

text: The doors of the heavens are opened for those who strive [in the way of Allah].

If the people who came before me complained about the injustice of their rulers, then today I complain about the injustice of my people; it is as if I am led and they are the leaders, [and] I am restrained and they are the restrainers.
The reward for striving [in the way of Allah] is the greatest reward.
And [Allah has prescribed] Jihād as [a means of preserving the] honour of Islam.
Strong determination and lavishness do not go together.
The purification of the body is [in] striving and fasting.
Indeed Jihād is the price of Paradise, so the one who struggles against his self will acquire it, and this is the greatest reward of Allah for the one who is cognizant of it.
The best Jihād is the struggle of a man against his [carnal] soul.
The best Jihād is the struggle of the self against lustful desires, and its weaning away from the pleasures of this world.
The first thing that you disavow from Jihād is struggling against your selves.
The last things that you [should] lose are: the struggling against your selves and obedience to those who have authority among you.
Indeed the best Jihād is the struggle of a man against his [carnal] soul.
Verily struggling against the self restrains it from sins and protects it from destruction.
Verily the one who struggles with his [lower] self, in obedience to Allah and against disobedience to Him, has the status of a virtuous martyr in the sight of Allah.

Indeed the one who struggles against his [lower] self, overcomes his anger and is careful in obeying [the commandments of] Allah, is raised by Allah, the Glorified, to the status of the one who fasts by day and stands in prayer by night, and is granted the rank of the patient soldier [who fights in His way].
Verily if you struggle against your [lower] self you will obtain the pleasure of Allah.
The fruit of struggle [against the self] is overpowering the self.
Struggling against the self is the dowry for Paradise.
Struggling against vain desires is the price of Paradise.
Struggling against the self is the best Jihad.
Struggle against your [lower] self and seek repentance, you will be successful in the obedience of your Lord.

Struggle against your vain desires, overcome your anger and resist your bad habits, [by this] your soul will become pure, your intellect will become perfect and the reward of your Lord will be complete.

Fight against your [lower] self in obedience to Allah the way an enemy would fight his enemy, and overpower it the way a rival would overpower his opponent, for indeed the strongest person is the one who subdues his self.

Struggle against your [lower] self and call it to account the way a partner would hold his partner accountable, and demand from it the right of Allah the way an adversary would demand from his foe, for verily the most felicitous of people is the one who undertakes to hold his self to account.
Struggling against the [lower] self is the price of Paradise, so the one who struggles against it will acquire it, and this is the greatest reward of Allah for the one who is cognizant of it.
Struggling against the self with knowledge is a symbol of intelligence.
Fighting anger with forbearance is evidence of nobility.
The most excellent Jihād is struggling against the self.
The highest form of struggle is for a man to struggle against his self.
It is sufficient for you, in your struggle against your [lower] self, that you always prevail over it and fight its vain desires.
One who fights his [lower] self perfects his piety.
One who knows his self struggles against it.
One who does not struggle against his self will not achieve victory.
There is no struggle more worthy than struggling against the self.
Struggling against the self is a trait of the noble ones.
Struggling against the self is a symbol of nobility.
Struggling against the self is the best Jihād.
There is no Jihād like struggle against the self.
Ignorance and miserliness are bad and harmful.
Ignorance in a human being is more harmful than gangrene [is] to the body.
Ignorance is a balky mount; whoever rides it stumbles and whoever accompanies it is led astray.
Ignorance of merits is one of the grossest demerits.
The greatest calamity is ignorance.
The worst ailment is ignorance.
The greatest ignorance is the ignorance of a person about himself.
The greatest ignorance is making enmity with the powerful, befriending the immoral and trusting the traitor.
Ignorance is a curse.
Ignorance is [a form of] death.
flag_note: Contains bracketed editorial insertion

text: People are enemies of that which they are ignorant of.
Ignorance is the most harmful foe.
Ignorance makes one stumble.
Ignorance spoils the Hereafter.
Ignorance is the [primary] source of evil.
flag_note: Contains bracketed editorial insertion

text: Ignorance is an ailment and a chronic disease.
Ignorance attracts peril.
Ignorance is the root of all evil.
Ignorance is the worst disease.
Ignorance corrupts all matters.
Ignorance makes one stumble and brings regret.
Ignorance causes the living to die and perpetuates misery.
Verily you will not attain any goal by ignorance, nor will you achieve any goodness by means of it, nor will you realize any of your wishes in the Hereafter through it.
It is through ignorance that every evil is instigated.
Many an ignorance is better than forbearance (or knowledge).
Ward off ignorance with knowledge.
Too much ignorance is destructive.
The worst affliction is ignorance.
Counter ignorance with knowledge.
The outcome of ignorance is loss; and the joy of the envious does not last.
The pinnacle of ignorance is for a person to brag about his ignorance.
Many a revered person has been humiliated by his ignorance.
Ignorance suffices as ignobility.
It suffices as ignorance for a person to be ignorant about himself.
It suffices as ignorance for a person to be pleased with himself.
It suffices as ignorance for a person to laugh without [a reason for] amusement.
It suffices as ignorance for a person to be ignorant of his limits [and standing in society].
It suffices as ignorance for a person to be ignorant of his flaw.
It suffices as ignorance for a person to be ignorant about his own faults and to malign people for that which he [himself] cannot turn away from.
It suffices as ignorance for a person to forbid people from that which he performs himself.
The language of ignorance is impoliteness.
One who gets uplifted by ignorance has opposed the intellect.
One who fights his ignorance with his knowledge succeeds with the most felicitous victory.
Being overcome by ignorance is one of the severest afflictions.
There is no poverty like ignorance.
With ignorance, no path is purified.
There is no poverty more severe than ignorance.
There is no abomination more disgraceful than ignorance.
There is no adversity more severe than ignorance.
The cornerstone of ignorance is animosity towards people.
An ignorant person is never found to be anything but falling short or excessive.
Neither does an ignorant restrain himself [from wrongdoing] nor does he benefit from good advice.
An ignorant person is one who obeys his vain desires in disobedience to his Lord.
The ignorant person feels aversion towards that which the wise person feels at ease with.
The ignorant person does not understand the learned because he [himself] was never learned before.
An ignorant person does not recognize his failure and does not accept the [good] advice given to him.
An ignorant person relies on his hopes and is negligent in his actions.
The ignorant person is like a rock through which water does not gush forth, and a tree, the branches of which do not become green, and a ground upon which foliage is not found.
An ignorant person is [like the] dead among the living.
The most wretched of all people is the ignorant one.
An unremorseful sinner is the most ignorant person.
The most ignorant person is one who is deceived by the praise of a flatterer who makes the ugly look appealing to him and makes him hate the [sincere] adviser.
The most hated creature in the sight of Allah is the ignorant person, because He deprived him of what He bestowed on His creation, and that is intellect.
Verily the ignorant is one whose ignorance leads astray and whose vain desires entice [towards evil]; so his speech is unhealthy and his action is blameworthy.
The ignorant one is perplexed.
The ignorant person inclines towards the one who is like him.
Man is an enemy of that which he is ignorant of.
The ignorant one does not restrain himself [from evil].
An ignorant person is a slave to his passions.
The ignorant person does not desist [from sinning].
An ignorant person seeks to raise himself but ends up abasing himself.
The ignorant person is one who is ignorant of his own capability.
An ignorant person is dead, even when he is alive.
The correctness of an ignorant person is like the mistake of a learned person (i.e. it happens rarely).
The ignorant person is deceived by [false] claims.
The ignorant person is one who is ignorant about his [own] affair.
The ignorant person is one who is deceived by his vain desires and his arrogance.
An ignorant person is one who takes his sincere advisor to be a deceiver.
When the ignorant one becomes stingy (or denies), he obtains [wealth] and when he obtains [wealth] (or professes belief in one God), he apostatizes.

text: Indeed the ignorant person is one who is enslaved by [worldly] pursuits.
When an ignorant person grows older, his ignorance rises.
The wealth of an ignorant person is in his worldly possessions and his hopes.
The reign of an ignorant person is like a stranger who [soon] moves to another place.
Many an ignorant person is saved by his ignorance.
The slip-ups of an ignorant person are excusable.
An ignorant king exposes his [own] flaws.
The worst person you can accompany is an ignorant one.
The correct [action] of an ignorant person is like the slip-up of an intelligent person.
The lost item of the ignorant person cannot be found.
Obedience to the foolish is a sign of ignorance.
Obedience to the foolish and being excessive [in speech or action] are two signs of ignorance.
The habit of the inexperienced [and ignorant] ones is to cut off the elements of favour.
The wealth of an ignorant person is in his worldly possessions.
The ignorant one is deceived by futile absurdities.
Every ignorant person is prone to temptation.1

text: For the ignorant there is loss in every situation.
One who is ignorant is disregarded [by others].
When one is ignorant, his consideration is reduced.
One who is ignorant of [a branch of] knowledge is hostile towards it.
One who does not know where he is placing his foot, trips.
One who is ignorant makes many blunders.
One who is ignorant becomes self-conceited; and his ‘today’ is worse than his ‘yesterday’.
It is from the nature of the ignorant to get angry quickly, in every situation.
No one antagonizes the learned like the ignorant [do].
Woe be to the one who persists in his ignorance and blessed is the one who realizes [his mistake] and finds the right course.
There is no independence for an ignorant person.
The ignorant one is not seen to be anything but immoderate (or excessive).
Nothing restrains the foolish except the edge of a sword.
Disobey the ignorant and you will be safe.
Hell is sufficient as a punishment.

He (‘a) said in his description of hell: [It is] a fire whose burning is intense, its roar is loud, its flames are rising, its blaze is incinerating, its groans are terrifying, its abatement is remote, its fuel is igniting, [and] its horrors are terrifying.

He (‘a) said while describing hell: Its inmate cannot leave, its prisoner cannot be released by ransom and its shackles cannot be broken. This abode has no fixed age so that it may perish, nor is there a lifespan for its inmates that they may pass away.
Verily all disbelieving schemers are inmates of the fire.
He (‘a) also said in his description of hellfire: Its pits are engulfed [with fire], its sides are pitch- dark, its vessels are scorching hot and everything about it is horrid.
None will be saved from the fire of hell except the one who abandons its actions (i.e. the actions that lead to it).
This tender skin does not have the tolerance to withstand the fire [of hell].
One who is afraid of hellfire keeps away from that which has been forbidden.
The inmates of hell are eternally tormented.
The one who enters hellfire is forever wretched.
The fuel of hellfire on the Day of Judgment will comprise of every rich person who was miserly towards the poor with his wealth and every learned scholar who sold his Hereafter for the world.
Be wary of the fire whose heat is intense, whose pit is deep and whose ornaments are made of [molten] iron.
Be wary of the fire whose tumultuous blaze is ready, its flames are intense and its torment is forever renewed.
Hellfire is the final end of the extremists.
Whoever loves us with his heart, supports us with his speech and fights our enemies with his sword, then he will be with us in Paradise at our stage.
Whoever loves us with his heart and supports us with his speech but does not fight alongside us with his hand, then he will be in Paradise but not at our stage.
Whoever loves us with his heart but pretends to hate us with his tongue will go to Paradise.
He who loves us should emulate our actions and clothe himself with piety.
One who loves us should prepare to be covered with afflictions.
One who befriends us should have a thick skin for tribulations [that will befall him].
Two types of people are destroyed because of me: the fanatic lover and the extreme hater.
If a mountain loved me, it would crumble.
Losing a loved one leads to forlornness.
One who loves you forbids you [from evil].
One who loves something speaks about it constantly.
Indeed only he who does not flatter you loves you, and only he who does not let you hear [his praise] praises you.
Let the most beloved person to you and the one who has the greatest status in your eyes be the one who strives hardest in benefiting people.
Let the most beloved person to you be the compassionate adviser.
The strength of the authority of evidence is stronger than the strength of the authority of force.
Allah, the Glorified, never leaves His servants without a necessary proof or an established, clear path.
Allah, the Glorified, does not leave His creation unheeded, nor does He neglect their affairs.
Allah, the Glorified, never lets His servants remain without a divinely appointed Prophet or a revealed book [to guide them].
One who is disproved has no right.

topic: The One who Presnts an Argument
text: The one who presents a strong argument may get support.

topic: The One who Presnts an Argument
text: One who argues by truth, succeeds.
The Hajj is a means of strengthening the religion.
Rage is a bout of insanity because its possessor regrets [afterwards], but if he does not feel regret, then his insanity is firmly established.
Repel [your] rage, think about the proof and protect yourself from nonsense - you will be safe from slip-ups.
One who is overly cautious may be destroyed.
Harm comes to the cautious one from his [own] place of security.
One who warns you is like the one who brings you glad tidings.
Soldiers [who fight for Islam] are the glory of religion and the bastions of [its] leaders.
Fleeing at the right moment is equivalent to victory in its time.
Soldiers are defenders of the people.
The bane of an army is opposing its commanders.
One who abandons his army has helped his adversaries.
Cast down your gaze in battles, for this will make you calmer and cause your hearts to be more tranquil.
Put the armoured man forward and the unarmoured one behind, and grit your teeth because this will make the swords skip off the skulls.
He who is frightened by what is in front of him retreats [and flees].
Defend [yourselves] with the edge of blades, charge forward [against the enemy] with your swords, give up your lives [for the sake of Allah] and walk towards death with calm.

By the one who splits the seed and creates the human being! They did not accept Islam, rather they succumbed to it [to remain safe] and hid their disbelief; and when they found supporters for it, they brought forth in the open that which they had hidden and made manifest that which they had concealed.

I swear by Allah! Even if you run away from the sword of this transitory world you will not be safe from the swords of the Hereafter. You are the foremost among the Arabs and the greatest figures [of the community], so be ashamed of fleeing [from the battlefield], for certainly in it is a covering of disgrace and [a cause of] entry into hellfire.
Do not fight against the one who seeks refuge in religion, for one who combats religion is ruined.
Do not combat the one who seeks the support of truth, for the one who fights the truth is [always] defeated.
Never seek to challenge anyone in combat, but if you are challenged, then respond; for the one who seeks it is an aggressor, and the aggressor is struck down.
Do not let the fleeing which is followed by return and the retreat that is followed by attack bear down

text: Give up your lives [for the sake of Allah] willingly and walk towards death with ease.

text: The best of arsenals is seeking support [from Allah].

text: Verily in fleeing [from the battlefield] there is the wrath of Allah, the Glorified, persistent disgrace and lasting shame; and certainly one who flees does not prolong his life, nor does he delay his day [of death].

text: Your intellects have decreased and your judgments have become fatuous. You are thus targets for the archer, morsels for the eater and easy prey for the hunter.

text: Keep returning to fight and be ashamed of fleeing [from the battlefield], for it is a disgrace for the progenies and [a cause of entry into] hellfire on the Day of Reckoning.

text: Grit your back teeth, for this makes the swords skip off the skull.

text: Fleeing [from the battle field] is one of the two humiliations.

text: Be ashamed of fleeing [from battle], for it is a disgrace for the progenies and [a cause of entry into] hellfire on the Day of Reckoning.

text: Twist the sides of the spears [while attacking], for this makes the spearheads move with more force.
One who opposes Allah is crushed.
One who fights against Allah is ruined.
Indeed, if you fight against Allah, you will be defeated and destroyed.
One who fights against the people will be fought and one who considers himself to be safe from plunder will be plundered.
The freeman is free even if hardship befalls him.
Liberty is free of malice and deception.
Sometimes the free man may be treated unjustly.
The free man will never become enslaved until distress is removed from him.

text: There is no reward for the free except honour [and respect].

text: Do not be a slave to others while Allah, the Glorified, has made you free, for that which is good is never achieved except by overcoming evil, and ease is never acquired except through difficulty.
One who is [overly] careful [not to put himself in any harm] is thrown [into it].
flag_note: Contains bracketed editorial insertions.

text: One whose carefulness increases, his unseen [future] becomes sound.
flag_note: Contains bracketed editorial insertions and the phrasing is unclear.

text: Greed is a disgrace and a humiliation for the one who espouses it.
Greed is the cornerstone of poverty and the foundation of evil.
Greed is one of the two miseries.
Greed, gluttony and stinginess are the result of ignorance.
Greed does not increase sustenance, rather it debases one’s status.
Take revenge on your greed through contentment, just as you would avenge your enemy by retaliation.
Be cautious of greed, for its possessor is subject to humiliation and suffering.
Be wary of greed, for it is a disgrace to the religion and the worst companion.
Verily in greed there is suffering.
Greed is the riding mount of hardship.
Greed is a sign of penury.
Greed has blameworthy consequences.
Greed is a symbol of the wretched.
Greed is [a trait that leads to] disgrace and suffering.
flag_note: contains bracketed editorial insertions

text: Greed corrupts conviction.
Greed humiliates and causes misery.
Greed is [a trait that results in] endless suffering.
flag_note: contains bracketed editorial insertions

text: Greed degrades magnanimity.
Greed leads to many flaws (or great sins).
flag_note: contains parenthetical editorial alternatives

text: Greed and gluttony earn wretchedness and humiliation.
Greed diminishes the status of a man and does not increase his sustenance.
Verily you cannot outrun your death, nor acquire that which is not for you, so why do you debase yourself O wretched one?!
It is through greed that hardship comes about.
The worst companion is greed.
The fruit of greed is hardship.
The fruit of greed is anguish.
Shunning greed severs gluttony and cupidity.
Intense greed comes from strong gluttony and weakness of faith.
Counter greed with contentment.
Yielding to greed corrupts certitude.
It is on doubt and lack of trust in Allah that greed and avarice are based.
The slave of greed is eternally wretched.
In greed there is hardship.
In greed there is misery and anguish.
Greed has been paired up with hardship.
Greed [is a mount that] kills its rider.
flag_note: Contains bracketed editorial insertions

text: Reduce your greed and remain [satisfied] with what has been allocated to you of your sustenance, [by this] you will protect your faith.
flag_note: Contains bracketed editorial insertions

text: How can there be relief from the suffering of greed for one who has not truly trusted [in Allah]?
flag_note: Contains bracketed editorial insertions

text: Too much greed makes its possessor miserable and abases him.
Not everyone who seeks, finds and not everyone who turns away, loses.
One who is greedy becomes wretched and undergoes hardship.
One whose greed increases, his status is lowered.
One who clothes himself with greed becomes poverty-stricken.
One whose greed increases, his certitude decreases.
One who is overcome by greed faces great humiliation.
Nothing debases the self like greed and nothing disgraces [one’s] honour like stinginess.
flag_note: Contains bracketed editorial insertions

text: How much agony is brought about by greed!
One who acts greedily is wretched and dispraised.
Do not let greed overpower your patience.
There is no [good] health with gluttony.
flag_note: Contains bracketed editorial insertions

text: A little greed leads to a lot of cupidity.
The one who is greedy is poor, even if he owns the whole world in its entirety.
The greedy one is [always] weary.
The greedy one is never satisfied.
The greedy person is a slave to [his] desires.
The greedy person toils for that which will harm him.
The glutton is never satisfied.
The greedy one is a prisoner of disgrace, never to be freed from his prison.
If you are greedy in your desire for that which has been guaranteed to you (i.e. your sustenance) then be avid in performing that which has been made incumbent upon you.
Many a greedy person has been killed by his greed.

I wonder at the one who knows that Allah has guaranteed sustenance and allotted it, and that his effort will not increase what has [already] been allotted for him of it, yet he is greedy and unrelenting in his desire for [more] wealth.
Every greedy person is needy.
Many a greedy person has been frustrated and many a contented person has not been disappointed!
There is no adequacy for a greedy person.
One who acts greedily is not bereft of indignity.
One whose greed increases, his wretchedness [also] increases.
One for whom greed of worldly possessions is coupled with stinginess has held fast to the two pillars of ignobility.
A greedy person has no shame.
A greedy person is never found relaxing.
Nothing makes one amass wealth except greed, and the greedy is wretched and dispraised.
The vocation [one undertakes] is based on the extent of deprivation.1
flag_note: The text contains bracketed editorial insertions and a trailing digit, suggesting an extraction error.

text: A [simple] vocation with modesty is better than affluence with immorality.
The prohibited is illicit.
Deprivation is abandonment.
I wonder at the person who hopes for favour from the one who is above him, how can he deprive the one who is below him [of his own favour]?
flag_note: The text contains bracketed editorial insertions.

text: The anguish of deprivation will not be calmed until acquisition is realized.
Do not deprive the distressed even if he is extravagant.
Do not frustrate the needy even if he insists [for more].
flag_note: The text contains bracketed editorial insertions.

text: Would you like to be among the victorious party of Allah? [Then] fear Allah, the Glorified, and be righteous in all your affairs, for surely Allah is with those who guard [against evil] and those who go good [to others].
flag_note: The text contains bracketed editorial insertions and a typo ('go good' instead of 'do good').

text: Judiciousness means enduring agony until the opportunity [to react] avails itself.
flag_note: The text contains bracketed editorial insertions.

text: The last sources of self-preservation are the first points of caution.
Judiciousness is considering the consequences [of actions] and consulting the wise.
flag_note: The text contains bracketed editorial insertions.

text: Indeed, the one who gets involved in matters without thinking about the consequences is vulnerable to grave calamities.
The root of determination is judiciousness, and its fruit is victory.
Judiciousness is a provision and negligence is a loss.
Judiciousness is a skill.
Judiciousness is [having] the most pertinent of views.
flag_note: The text contains bracketed editorial insertions.

text: Judiciousness is preserving the [lessons learned through] experience.
flag_note: The text contains bracketed editorial insertions.

text: Judiciousness is [achieved] through weighing the opinions thoroughly.
flag_note: The text contains bracketed editorial insertions.

text: Judiciousness is being extremely cautious.
Views are many but foresight is little.
Judiciousness is safeguarding that which you have been charged with and leaving that which has been guaranteed for you.
Tranquillity before [gaining] awareness [of the situation] is contrary to judiciousness.
Verily judiciousness is only in obedience to Allah and disobedience to the [lower] self.
The bane of judiciousness is losing the matter.
When judiciousness is coupled with determination, felicity becomes complete.
The fruit of judiciousness is wellbeing.
Act with judiciousness and cling to knowledge your results will be praiseworthy.
The end result of judiciousness is precaution.
The perfection of judiciousness is seeking to reform [one’s] opponents and being amicable with [one’s] enemies.
One who opposes judiciousness is destroyed.
One who acts judiciously is cautious.
One who fails to act with judiciousness is reckless.
One whose judiciousness is reduced, his determination is weakened.
One who is not pushed forward by judiciousness is held back by impuissance.
From judiciousness comes strong determination.
From judiciousness comes preparedness and readiness.
Preserving [the lessons learnt from] experience is from judiciousness.
Genuine determination comes from judiciousness.
Stopping [and assessing the situation] when faced with doubt is part of judiciousness.
From the excellence of judiciousness is being prepared to move and being ready to travel [from this world to the next].
The judicious person is one who does not get too preoccupied with the blessing [he has been given] to work for his afterlife.
The judicious person is one who is generous with what he has in his possession and does not postpone his work of today to tomorrow.
The judicious person is one who is not too preoccupied with the deceptions of his world to work for his Hereafter.
The judicious person is one who is amicable with [the people of] his time.
The judicious person is one who has been made worldly-wise by experience and refined by calamities.
The judicious person is one who gives thanks for blessings that come to him and is patient and thinks no more of it when the blessings turn away or turn back from him.
The judicious person is one who delays meting out punishment when [he is] under the yoke of anger and expedites the repayment of favours by taking advantage of the available opportunity.
The most judicious of you is the most abstemious of you [from worldly pleasures].
The most judicious of all people is one who deems his worldly affairs to be unimportant.
The most judicious of people is the one who presumes his inability despite having numerous supporters.
The most judicious of people is the one whose inner and outer garments are patience and consideration of the consequences [of his actions].
The most judicious of people is the one who fulfils his promise and does not postpone his work of today to tomorrow.
Indeed the judicious person is one who does not get beguiled by deceptions.

Verily the judicious person is one who occupies himself with struggling against his [lower] self, thereby rectifying it and preventing it from indulging in its vain desires and pleasures, thus he attains mastery over it; and verily for the intelligent one there is a preoccupation in keeping himself away from [that which is impermissible of] this world, its contents and its people.
Verily the judicious person is one who restrains his [lower] self by taking it to account, and controls it with rage (or by overcoming it), and kills it by fighting against it.
The judicious one is alert, the negligent one is sleepy.
The judicious person is one who does not harm others.
The judicious person is one who discards [excessive] expenses and luxuries.
The judicious person is one who abandons this world for the sake of the Hereafter.
The judicious is one who eschews extravagance and loathes waste.
Only he is judicious whose preoccupation is entirely with himself, whose concern is entirely for his religion, and whose struggle is entirely for his Hereafter.
Many a young person is more judicious than an old person.
The weapon of a judicious person is precaution.
In every action of the judicious person, there is merit.
The intellect of the judicious one acts as a deterrent from every demerit.
The judicious one does not become perplexed in times of adversity.
He who does not give generously from what he has and does not advance (or save) his work of today for his morrow1 is not a judicious person.

text: The judicious person never dispenses with a pertinent and superior opinion.

topic: Grief for what has been Lost
text: Do not grieve for that which is lost.
The reckoning is before the punishment and the reward is after the reckoning.
There is no beauty like high regard.
Jealousy is one of the two torments.
Jealousy is the viler of the two depravities.
Jealousy is an incurable disease, it does not end except by the destruction of the envier or the death of the envied.
Jealousy eats away good deeds just like fire consumes firewood.
Jealousy is a shameful flaw and a gross deficiency; one who possesses it is not cured except by realizing his hopes about the one whom he envies.
Be cautious of jealousy, for it disparages the self.
Be wary of jealousy for it is the worst quality, the ugliest attribute and the trait of the Devil.
Jealousy is stressful.
Jealousy is the worst of diseases.
Jealousy is imprisonment of the soul.
Jealousy is the principal of [all] flaws.
Jealousy makes life miserable.
Jealousy emaciates (and exhausts) the body.
Jealousy melts away the body.
Jealousy gives rise to depression.
Jealousy is the great trap of the Devil.
Jealousy is an ailment that cannot be cured.
Jealousy is the habitude of the vile ones and the enemies of fortunes.
When jealousy between the people rains, corruption grows.
The fruit of jealousy is wretchedness in this world and the Hereafter.
Shun jealousy, dishonesty and malice, for indeed these three [characteristics] disgrace the religion and destroy the person [who possesses them].
The cornerstone of [all] depravities is jealousy.
The cause of depression is jealousy.
The weapon of ignobility is jealousy.
The worst thing that can accompany a person is jealousy.
Purify your hearts of jealousy, for it is a depressing enfeebler.
Just as rust corrodes iron until it causes it to waste away, so too does jealousy corrode the body until it wears away.
Jealousy is not from the characteristics of the God-wary.
Jealousy towards a friend for the blessing [he has been endowed with] stems from low self- esteem.1
flag_note: Contains stray citation character at the end of the sentence.

text: Woe be to jealousy, how fair it is! It starts off with its companion and then kills him.
Do not be jealous of each other, for jealousy eats away the faith like fire consumes firewood; and do not have hatred for one another for this is severing [for the faith].
There is no malady like jealousy.
Happiness does not last for the jealous and the spiteful.
The jealous one is always ill and the miser is always abased.
The jealous one is always sick, even when his body is healthy.
The jealous person is always ill.
The jealous one is never cured.
The jealous one never gains authority.
The jealous one is angry at destiny.
The jealous one has many regrets and his sins are multiplied.
When blessings are [openly] displayed, the enviers increase.
I am amazed at the heedlessness of the jealous about the health of their bodies.
The jealous one has no friendship.
One whose jealousy increases, his depression becomes prolonged.
How little comfort the jealous person has!
Because of the favour of Allah upon you, do not be jealous.
There is no comfort for the jealous.
The jealous person will never be found happy.
A believer is never jealous.
No life is more miserable than the life of the jealous and the spiteful.
The jealous person is never pleased with the one whom he is jealous of except by [his] death or cessation of the blessing.
It is a consolation for you that the one who is jealous of you becomes furious when you are happy.
For the jealous one, there is no friendship.
For the jealous one, there is no cure.
The jealous person considers the cessation of a blessing from the person whom he envies to be a blessing upon himself.
It is amazing how heedless the jealous are of the health of the bodies!
The jealous person displays his affection in his words and hides his hatred in his actions; he has the title of a friend and the attribute of an enemy.
The jealous one is happy with disaster [befalling others] and saddened by [their] happiness.
Nothing cures the jealous one but cessation of the blessing.
Every person of high rank is envied.
At times even a good steed may stumble.
At times the [sharp] sword becomes blunt.
Acquiring of good deeds is one of the best of earnings.
For every good deed there is recompense.
In every good deed there is reward.
Every good deed which is not done with the intention of seeking nearness to Allah, has the ugliness of ostentation in it and its fruit is an ugly requital.
Showing kindness to the enemy is one of the two triumphs.
Following up one favour with another favour is from the perfection of munificence.
Doing good is the nature of the righteous and doing evil is the nature of the wicked.
Benevolence from the wicked corrupts just as much as it reforms from the honourable.
If a righteous act is not nurtured, it wears away, just like worn out garments and dilapidated buildings.
Do good and you shall enthral.
Bestow goodness and you shall advance.
Do good and you will be thanked.
Forget your gift, [and] remember your promise.
Give and you shall become capable (or be chosen).
Give generously and you shall gain authority.
Confer favours and you will be praised.
Extend your goodness and do no harm.
Be good [to others] and good will be done to you.
Be good to the evildoer and you will dominate him.
Bestow favours on the people and your status will increase.
Show kindness to whomever you wish and you will become his master.
Confer favours and you will be thanked, fear [Allah] and you will be feared [by the people] and do not crack [silly] jokes such that you are belittled.
Seize the opportunity to perform righteous deeds and be careful of your obligations towards your brothers.
Start by giving the one who has not asked you, and extend your favour to the one who has sought it, and be cautious never to turn away a beggar.
Donate your wealth generously towards righteous works and support your friend[s] with it, for indeed generosity is a more befitting trait for the free.
Do good to the one who is under your authority and the one under whose authority you are will do good to you.
The best faith is [that which is accompanied by] righteousness.
The best favours are those that correspond with divinely ordained laws.
The best act is that which benefits the pious ones.
The best act is that which benefits those who are deserving of it.
The merit of a righteous action is better than the action [itself].
The greatest righteous act is establishing ties with near relatives.
The most beautiful act of a person in a position of power is conferring of favours [to those under him].
The best treasure is a free man who has been reserved [in your friendship because of your kindness to him].
The greatest good deed is supporting one’s brothers [financially].
The best gift is forgoing obligation.
The noblest of favours are the good turns of the munificent [and honourable] ones.
The most worthy of giving [to] is the one who feels the least in need of asking [from others].
The best grant is that which is given before it is sought.
The most pleasing kindness is offering [something] without being asked [for it].
The best grant is that which is [bestowed] before the humility of having to ask [for it].
The best of all people who have preceded you is the one who has preceded you in his good expectation of you.
The most worthy of favour among the people is one who is patient when he is put off, excuses when he is denied and shows gratitude when he is given.
Of all people, the most worthy of doing good to others is the one upon whom Allah has bestowed favours and granted with the ability [to do good to others].
The most worthy of bestowing favours [to others] is the one upon whom numerous favours of Allah have been bestowed.
Verily the good act that brings reward quickest is the act of kindness.
Verily giving away this wealth is an acquisition [for the Hereafter] and withholding it is an affliction.
Verily spending this wealth in obedience to Allah is the greatest blessing and spending it in disobedience to Him is the greatest tribulation.
Indeed extending greetings is from sublime morals.
Verily Allah, the Glorified, loves everyone who is open-handed and strong in faith.
Verily the value of asking is greater than the worth of what is given, so do not regard that which you give as much, for it will never be equal to the humiliation of asking.
Verily the little that is from Allah, the Glorified, is more valuable than the plenty [that is gotten] from His creatures.
Verily the good turn that you did to one of the people was only a means to ennoble yourself and embellish your honour, so do not seek gratitude from others for that which you did for yourself.

Indeed your goodness towards the ones who plots against you from your opponents and enviers is more irritating for them than your trying to do them harm, and it is [also] a means of inviting them to reform [themselves].
Verily your munificence does not extend to all of the creation, so aim it towards the noblest of creation.
It is not from the practice of the virtuous to delay the bestowal of favours.
Benevolence is authority.
Benevolence is distinction.
Kindness is [a cause of] love.
Benevolent acts are loans.
Doing good [to others] is beneficial.
Benevolence is merit, munificence is nobility.
Benevolence is a treasure.
The human being is a slave of kindness.
Benevolence is the alms-tax for blessings.
Benevolent acts are the best booty.
Kindness is the pinnacle of excellence.
Kindness enslaves (or enthrals) human beings.
Benevolence is the most honourable authority.
The evil deed is erased by a benevolent act.
Merit is [acquired] with benevolence.
Conferring favours is the most excellent munificence.
Benevolence is an everlasting reserve.
Kindness is a treasure and the munificent is one who obtains it.
People are the followers of what they deem to be good.1

text: The good turn done by an intelligent (or an honourable) person is most excellent [in] merit.
The favour of an ignoble person is the worst depravity.
Rewarding good with evil is [the highest form of] ingratitude.
Benevolence is the most thriving cultivation and the best treasure.
Doing good to the one who offends you is the most excellent merit.
A benevolent act is sullied by repeatedly putting one under obligation through it.
Doing good to the honourable ones is the best provision and the noblest deed.
Doing good to the one who offends [you] reforms the enemy.
Benevolence is a treasure so consider whom you are leaving it with.
Righteous work is a provision, so be wary of whom you are placing it with.
If you confer favours, you will be served.
Verily if you do good [to others] then you are [actually] honouring your own soul and doing good to it.
Verily you are more in need of doing good to the people than of accumulating wealth.
The bane of giving is procrastination.
When you perform a good turn then conceal it.
When a good turn has been done to you then publicize it.
When you [wish to] give, be quick.
When a good turn is done to you, recall it.
When you do a good turn [to someone], forget it.
If you do good to a vile person, he will wrong you in return for your goodness to him.

I am free to choose with regards to the one upon whom I have not bestowed any favour but am bound to complete my favour on the one upon whom I have bestowed it; for if I complete it, I will have preserved it and if I cut it off then I will have lost it, and if I lose it then why did I embark on it [in the first place]?
If your bounty falls short of reaching the weak, then [at least] let your mercy reach them.

If you find from the needy people one who will carry your provision for you up to the Day of Resurrection and return it to you tomorrow when you need it most, then take the opportunity and give it to him, and increase the provisions that you give him [to carry for you] while you are able to, for it is possible that you may [at one time] seek him but not find him.
Through kindness, human beings are enslaved.
Through benevolence, gratitude lasts.
Through kindness, hearts are owned.
Through kindness, freemen are owned.
Through kindness and covering faults with forgiveness, eminence increases.
Through kindness, people are enthralled.
Giving generously is the alms-tax of blessings.
Extending the hand in giving is the most beautiful virtue and the most excellent trait.
Stretching out the hand in giving increases reward and multiplies recompense.
Expediting good turns is the basis of righteousness.
Wasting benevolence is showing it to someone who does not comprehend [its value].
Do good [to people] and you will be served; be forbearing (or gain knowledge) and you will advance.
The completion of benevolence is abandoning [putting one under] obligation by it.
The peoples’ expectation of your kindness is better than their fear of your retribution.
Adorn yourselves by taking up kindness, stopping transgression, acting upon the truth, being just and impartial, keeping away from corruption and improving your Hereafter.
The beauty of benevolence is [in] relinquishing obligation.
The beauty of a benevolent act is in completing it.
Denying a favour instigates the ugliness of obligation.
Denying the benevolence [of others] leads to deprivation.
The best good turn is one that benefits the righteous.
The best benevolent act is one that is neither preceded by delay nor followed by obligation.
The best grant is that which is [given] without being sought.
Act with kindness towards your enemy for this is one of the two triumphs.
Whoever bestows favours on others, they are thankful for his authority.
Whoever shows benevolence, his habit is praised.
The pinnacle of kindness is being kind to the believers.
The pinnacle of generosity is being expeditious in giving.
The pinnacle of faith is doing good to people.
The pinnacle of excellence is doing good to the virtuous.
The pinnacle of depravity is doing good to the wicked.
Nurturing a good turn is better than starting it.
Increase your benevolent acts and bestow more favours, for this is a more lasting provision and a more beautiful legacy.
The cause of affection is benevolence.
Continuous bestowal [of favours] is the practice of the honourable.
Ask for good from one who forgets it and do good to the one who recalls it.
The worst grant is that which is preceded by delay and followed by obligation.
Performing benevolent actions protects one from falling into disgrace.
Doing good turns is from the merits of the human being.
Performing benevolent actions causes the abundant flow of blessings and wards off calamity.
The good turn of wealth ceases with its cessation.
Blessed is the one who does good to the servants [of Allah] and prepares provisions for the Hereafter.
He who does a good turn to those who are undeserving of it has oppressed it.
The one who confers his favours to the honourable ones acquires the most sublime gains.
Espouse kindness, for it is the best cultivation and the most profitable merchandise.
Be good to the servants [of Allah] and act justly in the lands, [by this] you will safe when the witnesses are presented [on the Day of Judgment].
Perform benevolent works, for they are the best provisions for the Hereafter.
Perform benevolent acts and do good to your near relatives and neighbours, for these two actions prolong life and make the lands prosper.
By successive acts of kindness and benevolence, the free man is enslaved.
The habit of benevolence is the source of capability [or power].
I am amazed at the one who buys slaves with his wealth, how can he not buy the freemen with his benevolence, thereby enthralling them.
In every [act of] benevolence there is kindness.
In every good turn there is indebtedness.
Sometimes it is better to give in order to fulfil a promise [and not delay it].

text: Send your good turn ahead [for the Hereafter] and you will benefit.
flag_note: Contains bracketed editorial commentary/reconstruction within the text.

text: Every [form of] benevolence is a favour.
flag_note: Contains bracketed editorial commentary/reconstruction within the text.

text: How many a human being has been enslaved by benevolence!
Increased rendering of benevolent works prolongs life and spreads renown.
Doing a lot of good turns raises one’s honour and makes gratitude last.
The guarantee of continued affluence and capability [and power] is [in] following up one favour with another favour.
flag_note: Contains bracketed editorial commentary/reconstruction within the text.

text: Everything has a merit and the merit of the honourable ones is doing good to the people.
Let your traits be generosity and benevolence.
One cannot show gratitude for blessings in a better way than using them to benefit others.
If you were to see benevolence in the form a person, you would surely see him as a beautiful form that surpasses the worlds [in its beauty].
One who bestows goodness [to others] is served [by them].
One who generously gives [from] his wealth becomes great.
flag_note: Contains bracketed editorial commentary/reconstruction within the text.

text: One who bestows favours fulfils the right of authority.
One who puts others under obligation for his favour, spoils it.
One who extends his goodness [to the people] deserves leadership.
One who renders a beautiful deed acquires great praise.
One who performs a benevolent action gains reward and gratitude.
One who cuts off his usual favours, Allah will cut off his present capabilities.
One who does not bestow favours will not achieve nobility.
One who does not give while he is sitting [in comfort] will not be given when he is standing [in a state of struggle].
One who does not give while he is sitting [in ease] will be deprived when he is standing [in adversity].
One who favours an ignorant person demonstrates the extent of his own ignorance.
One who conceals the favour [that has been done to him] is punished with deprivation.
One who withholds favours is stripped of [his] ability.
One who does good to a freeman gains a [great] reward.
One who does a kind act earns good praise.
One whose benefactions are abundant demonstrates his great nobility.
One whose kindness is abundant is loved by his brothers.
Whoever extends his goodness [to others], more people are inclined towards him.
One who accepts your gift has [actually] assisted you in gaining honour.
One who perfects his kindness gives generously before he is asked.
One who does good to the undeserving has wronged his goodness.
One who gives in cases that are undeserving fails to give [the rights] to those who are deserving.
One who is ungrateful for a good turn deserves an ugly separation.
One who reciprocates a good turn with a better one has [appropriately] repaid it.
One whose benefaction increases, his assistants and helpers [also] increase.
Whoever extends his benevolence [to others], the hearts become inclined towards him.
One who grants generously before being asked, then he is truly honourable and much-loved.
One who repays goodness with evil has rid himself of magnanimity.
Whoever does good to the people, their love for him lasts.
One who fulfils the [debt of] goodness that was done to him in the past has attained true freedom.
One who turns to you hopefully has already got a good impression of you, so do not disappoint his expectation.
Whoever fulfils the rights of one who does not fulfil his rights has enslaved him.
One who is kind to the people, his outcomes become good and the ways [to his goals] become easy for him.
Whoever accepts a good turn has made the one who rendered it to him his master.
One who accepts your good turn has made his right over you mandatory [on himself].
Whoever does good to the one who does evil to him has taken the all-encompassing excellence.
One who is not grateful for favours is not spared from deprivation.
One who begins giving without being asked and completes good deeds without any obligation has perfected his favour.
One who bestows a favour on the ungrateful one prolongs his rage.
One who is generous in granting [favours], enthrals the people of this world.
One who does not nurture his good turn has indeed lost it.
One who accepts your good turn has sold you his honour and magnanimity.
One who accepts your good turn has humbled his prestige and honour before you.
Whoever does not nurture his favour, then it is as if he did not bestow it.
Doing good to others is part of an honourable purpose.
One of the greatest afflictions is wasting good turns [on the undeserving].
One of the best favours is the favour that is done to the righteous.
Nothing earns gratitude like doing good to others.
Nothing enthrals people like doing [them] favours.

No one has appealed to me with an intercession that is greater in my sight than a favour that I had previously done to him, so that I may nurture it and follow it up with another [favour] like it; for indeed later refusals cut off the gratitude for earlier favours.
The basis of goodness is abandoning obligation through it.
flag_note: The text is syntactically garbled and lacks clear meaning.

text: With goodness [to others], there is loftiness.
Nurturing a good turn [and completing it] is better than starting it [anew].
How good a store [for the future] benevolence is!
The best provision for the Hereafter is doing good to the people.
Achievement of glorious feats is through performing noble deeds.
Never regard what you give as too much, even if it is plenty, for indeed the good praise [you will get for your generosity] will be greater than it.
Never regard what you give as great, even if it is substantial, for indeed the extent of [humiliation undergone through] begging is greater than that.
One who does not show kindness [to others] in times of fortune will be abandoned in times of misfortune.
Whoever places his goodness with the one who does not deserve it has wasted it.
Doing a good turn to those who deserve it subdues the enemy and protects from falling into evil.
Never show your benevolence to the one who does not understand its value (or who is not good).
Do not do a good turn to the one who is ungrateful for your kindness.
Never hold back an act of benevolence, even if you do not find one who understands its value.
Do not be ashamed of giving little, for not giving at all is even less than that.
Never regard the abundance of what you have given to be much, for you are [in possession of] even more than that.
Never hold back from doing good turns and favours thereby being stripped of [your] ability.
Do not delay giving the needy to tomorrow, for you do not know what will happen to you or to him tomorrow.
Let not your brother be stronger in his iniquity towards you than you are in your goodness [towards him].

Never let the paucity of those who show gratitude for your benevolence deter you from it, for you have been thanked by the One who does not benefit from any of it; and more may be gained from the gratitude of the thankful than what is neglected by the ingrate.
Do not help [anyone] against the one who has favoured you, for the one who helps against the one who has favoured him is stripped of his ability.
Goodness does not thrive with the ignoble.
The wicked do not do good to anyone except those who are like them.
There is no merit loftier than benevolence.
There is no virtue greater than benevolence.
There is no benevolence more misused than doing good to the ingrate.
There is no virtue in doing good to one who does not know its value.
A good turn does not benefit except with one who possesses loyalty and self-restraint.
Giving little is better than offering excuses [for not giving].
Good turns do not thrive except with the honourable.
There is no virtue in the good turn that is reckoned [as a favour].
The consequences of kindness are never dispraised.
None is praised except the one who shows his kindness.
It is enough of a donation to give what is [readily] available.
Benevolence is the better of the two treasures.
Good turns are shackles that cannot be extricated except through gratitude or requital.
Completing a good turn is better than starting it.

A benevolent action is not completed except by three things: by taking it to be insignificant, by expediting it and by concealing it; for when you take it to be insignificant, you have made it great; and when you expedite it, you have made it beneficial; and when you conceal it, you have made it complete.
Doing a good turn is the best acquisition [for the Hereafter], and generosity is the best ornament.
When the kind people become fewer, those who adorn themselves get ruined.
By doing good to others, ranks get elevated.
By conferring favours, people are enthralled.
Through [his] abundant favours, the munificent person is recognized.
By conferring favours [to others], [one’s] faults are hidden.
Give life to your good deed by killing it (i.e. by forgetting it).
Do good whenever possible, and deter the evildoer with righteous action.
Extend your benevolence to all the people, for verily nothing can be equated with the virtue of a good turn in the sight of Allah, the Glorified.
Give life to the benevolent act by killing it (i.e. forgetting it), for verily the sense of obligation destroys a good turn.
The best good deed is coming to the aid of the aggrieved.
The loftiest good turn is that which is done to those who deserve it.
The best favour of the wicked person is holding back his harm [from others].
The ugliest deed of an honourable person is withholding his contribution.
Verily the people who do good [to others] are more in need of doing it than those who request it from them.
Benevolence is [a means of] servitude.
The most profitable wares are the rendering of benevolent actions.
The perfection of giving is in expediting it.
The human being is not enthralled until he is engulfed by favour.
One who is not good at seeking sympathy is faced with scorn.2

text: Nothing enthrals the honourable ones like benevolence.
The best of treasures are: the good turn that is consigned to (or by) the free and the knowledge that is learned by the virtuous.
Ingratitude for favours leads to deprivation.
One who withholds from giving is deprived of (or prevents) praise.
Giving after having refused is more graceful than refusing after having given.
Whoever does good to the people, Allah covers him with His mercy and places him in His pardon.
Give whatever you are giving expeditiously and beneficially, and if you refuse then let it be with politeness and apology.
One who finds it easy to give away [his] wealth has hopes directed towards him.
One who loves to be remembered with praise should give generously from his wealth.
One who gives generously enthrals the people.
Nothing spreads renown like generosity.
Generosity is the expander of ability.
Generosity earns praise.
Through generosity, praises are increased.
By being generous with blessings, the blessings last longer.
Increased generosity is a sign of nobility.
Let not the good doer and the evildoer be equal in your eyes, for will make the good-doer abstain from his benevolence and will encourage the evildoer to continue his evil.

text: The charitable one needs the beggar.
Be open-handed but do not be wasteful.
The good doer person is one who is benevolent to all people.
The benevolent is supported, the malevolent is scorned.
The good doer is one whose words are affirmed by his actions.
The benevolent one is alive, even if he is transferred to the dwellings of the dead.

If you rush towards good whenever you see it, distance yourself from evil when you see it, act obediently [upon the commandments of Allah] and vie to acquire noble traits, then you are righteous and successful.
The worst of the benevolent ones is the one who puts others under obligation by his favour.
The doer of good deeds does not stumble, and when he does stumble, he finds a support [to hold on to].
Every good doer is affable.
The good doers are recognized by what the righteous people speak about them, and by their good deeds and virtuous conduct.
Physical beauty is of no benefit without nobility.

topic: Dyslogia (The Inability to Express Oneself Effectively)
text: The ugliness of dyslogia is better than the harm of talking nonsense.

topic: Dyslogia (The Inability to Express Oneself Effectively)
text: The inability of effective expression weakens the argument.

topic: Dyslogia (The Inability to Express Oneself Effectively)
text: Dyslogia is better than babble.
The fortune of a person that comes through the ears is for himself and that which is on the tongue for others.
Fortune rushes towards the one who does not seek it.
Favour is gained in the sight of the Creator by yearning for that which is with Him; favour is gained with the creatures by turning away from what they possess.

topic: Digging a Pit for a Brother
text: One who digs a pit for his brother, Allah will cause him to fall in his [own] pit.

topic: Digging a Pit for a Brother
text: One who digs a pit for his believing brother will fall into it [himself].
Malice is from the nature of the wicked.
Spite is a fire that is not put out except by vanquish. (It is a raging fire that is not put out by anything other than death or vanquish).
flag_note: Contains parenthetical text that suggests a redundant or alternative translation, indicating an extraction error.

text: Malice wears away [its possessor].
Spite is the trait of the jealous ones.
Malice is the motive of rage.
Spite is the vilest of flaws.
Malice is a painful ailment and an infectious disease.
Malice is a vile characteristic and a fatal sickness.

Keep away from harbouring grudges against each other, hating each other, quarrelling with one other and not lending a supporting hand to each other, [and by doing this] you will gain mastery over your affairs.
The cornerstone of flaws is spite.
The cause of discord is malice.
The weapon of evil is spite.
The worst thing that resides in the heart is malice.
Extreme malice stems from the intense jealousy.
Purify your hearts from malice, for it is an infectious disease.
In times of difficulty, feelings of malice disappear.
One who eliminates malice [from his heart], his heart and mind become relaxed.
There is no brotherhood for the spiteful.
One whose spite increases, his censure decreases.
One who sows hatred reaps tribulations.
How miserable is the life of a spiteful person!
The spiteful person has no love.
The spiteful one has a tormented soul is doubly distressed.
