text: There is no repose for the spiteful.
Do not belittle anyone until you have heard from him.
There is no action like verification.
There is no practice better than verification.
Truth is an incisive sword.
Truth is the best way.
Truth is the strongest supporter.
Truth is the clearest course.
The truth is worthier of being followed.
Assisting one another to establish the truth is [a sign of] trustworthiness and faith.
Truth is a sword [to fight] against the followers of falsehood.
Truth is a refuge for every worker (and an argument for every speaker).
Through truth, the petitioner gets support.
It is by turning away from the truth that misguidance comes about.
By clinging to the truth, support is received.
There is truth and falsehood, and each has its followers.
Truth that harms is better than falsehood that brings joy.
Plunge into hardships to [arrive at] the truth wherever it may be.
flag_note: Contains bracketed editorial insertions

text: May Allah have mercy on the person who supports truth when he sees it, repels injustice when he sees it and assists his companion by truth.
May Allah have mercy of the person who enlivens the truth, causes falsehood to die, fights against oppression and establishes justice.
flag_note: Grammatical error in source text ('mercy of the person' instead of 'mercy on the person')

text: The peak of wisdom is clinging to the truth and obeying the one who stands for the truth.
Seeking assistance to establish the truth is [a sign of] faith and uprightness.
flag_note: Contains bracketed editorial insertions

text: Cling to the things that necessitate the [establishment of] truth and beware of the things that transpose falsities [to make them seem true].
flag_note: Contains bracketed editorial insertions

text: Your return to the truth is better than your persisting in falsehood.
Your returning to the truth, even if you get exhausted, is better than your comfort while clinging to falsehood.
In adhering to the truth, there is prosperity.
Abandon the one who has abandoned the truth for other than it, and leave him and that which he has preferred for himself.
Little truth repels much falsehood, just as a little fire burns a lot of firewood.
Speak the truth and you will benefit; do not utter falsehood and you will be safe.
For truth there is stability.
Let your refuge be the truth, for verily truth is the strongest supporter.
One who does not act upon the truth will never attain salvation.
One who acts upon the truth, gains [from it].
flag_note: Contains unnecessary bracketed editorial insertion

text: One who acts upon the truth, profits.
One who acts upon the truth is saved.
One who acts upon the truth becomes successful.
One who fights against the truth is thrown down.
One who speaks truthfully is believed.
One who tries to prevail against the truth is overpowered [by it].
One who battles against the truth is ruined.
One who opposes the truth is killed (or thrown down) by it.
One who opposes the truth is seized by powerlessness.
One who opposes the truth has taken Allah as his adversary.
One who is not saved by the truth is destroyed by falsehood.
One who transgresses the truth, his path becomes narrowed.
One who seeks honour through truth will be honoured by truth.
One who shows his face [in opposition] to the truth is destroyed.
One who takes the truth as his reins, the people will take him to be their leader.
Whoever acts upon the truth, the creation incline towards him.
One who feels ashamed of speaking the truth is really a fool.
One who struggles to establish the truth is granted success [by Allah].
One who deviates from the truth, his end is dispraised.
Whoever surrenders to the truth and follows the rightful [leader] is [considered to be] among the righteous.
Whoever makes the truth his goal, difficult things are made easy for him and distant things are brought nearer to him.
Whoever weakens the truth and forsakes it is destroyed by falsehood and killed by it.
One whose goal is the truth will attain it, even if he is very uncertain.
Whoever opposes the truth, it kills him and whoever tries to overpower it, it humiliates him.
Whoever helps the truth, benefits.
How numerous are those who admit to the truth but do not follow it!
One who contends with the truth is defeated.
How good a guide truth is!
Do not hold back from presenting the truth when you find those who are worthy of it.
Let nothing make you feel at ease but the truth and let nothing make you uneasy except falsehood.
Let not your attention towards the rights of a person [who is close to you] prevent you from establishing justice against him.
Falsehood and truth do not go together.
None is patient in the face of truth except the judicious and intelligent one.
There is no messenger more conveying than the truth.
There is no adviser more sincere than the truth.
There is no companion who is dearer than the truth.
One who takes the support of truth is not defeated.
One who argues by truth is not defeated.
One who elevates himself by truth is not overtaken (or abased).
None is patient with the truth except the one who knows its merit.
A man cannot be faulted for taking his right, rather he can only be censured for taking that which is not [rightfully] his.
A little truth repels much falsehood.
[About the ones who did not participate in the battle]: They forsook the truth and did not assist the falsehood.
The truth is illuminated and free from prejudice and hypocrisy.
Act upon the truth even if is against your desires and do not sell your Hereafter for this world.
Cling to the truth and it will take you to the place of the followers of truth, on the day when judgment will not be made except with truth.
Cling to the truth and salvation will cling to you.
Recognize the right of the one who knows your right, [be he] young or old, inferior or superior.
Indeed, one who is not benefitted by the truth is harmed by falsehood, and one who is not set straight by guidance is dragged down by misguidance.
The biggest loser is one who is able to speak the truth but still does not speak it.
The best of creation are those who judge more with truth, and the most beloved among them in the sight of Allah are those who are more truthful in speech.
One who is overcome [while he is] on the right, is victorious.
One who wages war against the truth is ruined.
Speaking the truth is better than inarticulateness and silence.

topic: One who is on the Right
text: The goal of one who is on the right is [following or remaining on] the right course.

topic: The Rights of Allah, The Most High
text: Giving this wealth in order to fulfil the rights of Allah has been made part of generosity.

topic: The Rights of Allah, The Most High
text: Take out the [rightful] dues from your wealth and share in your wealth with your friend; let your speech be measured and your endeavour well thought-out, [for by this] you will remain safe from censure and regret.

topic: The Rights of Allah, The Most High
text: The right of Allah, the Glorified, upon you in times of ease is piety and gratitude, and in times of hardship, [to have] contentment and patience.
Allah, the Glorified, has placed the rights of His servants before His rights, so whoever fulfils the rights of the servants of Allah, then this helps one to fulfil the rights of Allah.
The stingy hoarder accumulates for the one who does not thank him (i.e. his heirs) and proceeds towards the one who will not accept his excuse (i.e. Allah).
Hoarding is a vice.
Hoarding invites deprivation.
The hoarder is deprived of his blessing.
It is from the nature of the inexperienced [and ignorant] to trouble the people by hoarding.
Be solvent (or an assessor), and do not be a hoarder.
Hoarding is the practice of the vicious.
In impelling the servants of Allah to follow (or in their acting upon) the ordinances of Allah, there is the fulfilment of rights and all of kindness.
If you were to preserve the bounds of Allah, the Glorified, He would hasten for you His promised bounty.
One who neglects the commandments of freedom is made to return to serfdom.
Wisdom is a garden for the intelligent and a promenade for the noble.
Wisdom does not settle in the heart of a hypocrite except that it departs from it [soon after].
Wisdom is the lost property of every believer, so take it even if it be from the mouths of hypocrites.
Wisdom is a tree that grows in the heart and bears [its] fruit on the tongue.
Fill your heart with wisdom and don the attire of tranquillity for these two are the ornaments of the virtuous.
The beginning of wisdom is abandoning [worldly] pleasures and its end is loathing the transitory.
The greatest wisdom is for the human being to know himself and to remain within his limits.
Wisdom guides [one] to the right.
Wisdom is protection.
Wisdoms are the gardens of the noble ones.

When you get lost from the wisdom of Allah then stand with His power, for indeed [even] if you do not get of His wisdom that which can heal you, you will not lose of His power that which will suffice you.
Through wisdom, the veil of knowledge is removed.
The fruit of wisdom is success.
The fruit of wisdom is disdain for the world and infatuation with the Eternal Paradise.
The beauty of wisdom is kindness and good amicability.
The boundary of wisdom is turning away from the perishing abode [of this world] and being infatuated with the Eternal Abode [of the Hereafter].
The wisdom of a lowly person elevates him and the ignorance of a respectable person degrades him.
Take wisdom from wherever it may be, for verily wisdom is the lost property of every believer.
Take wisdom from the one who brings it to you, and look at what he is said and do not look at who said it.
flag_note: Grammatical error in the phrase 'look at what he is said'

text: The embellishment of wisdom is being uninterested in the pleasures of this world.
The lost possession of an intelligent person is wisdom, so he is more entitled to it wherever it may be.
The lost possession of a sage is wisdom, so he seeks it out wherever it may be.
Espouse wisdom, for indeed it is an exquisite ornament.
The prize of the sagacious is learning wisdom.
Sometimes words of wisdom may be uttered by one who is not wise.
Wisdom has been paired with protection [from sins].
Everything leads to weariness except novel wisdom.
How can one be patient in disassociating from the enemies [of his felicity] when he is not aided by wisdom?
Every time wisdom grows stronger, lust grows weaker.
Acquiring wisdom is [a means of] beautifying speech and employing kindness.
One who enjoys the insights of wisdom is not bereft of delight.
One who attaches himself to wisdom has ennobled himself.
One who is known for [his] wisdom is looked at with reverence.
One whose wisdom becomes established understands the lessons [that can be learnt from the past].
From the treasures of the unseen comes forth wisdom.
It is part of wisdom to obey the one who is above you, to respect those who are at your level and to be fair to those who are below you.

It is from [the dictates of] wisdom that you should not dispute with the one who is above you; you should not humiliate the one who is below you; you should not pursue that which is not in your ability; you should not let your tongue go against [what is in] your heart, nor let your words go against your deeds; you should not speak about that which you have no knowledge of; and you should not leave the matter when it comes in front of you and seek it when it has passed.
Gatherings of wisdom are the plantations of the praiseworthy.
Lustful desire and wisdom do not go together.
Wisdom does not reside in a heart [that is filled] with lust.
There is no wisdom except with safeguarding [from sin].
The wise are the most honourable of all people, the most patient of them, the quickest of them in forgiving and the best of them in character.
The wise person cures the asker [of his ignorance] and is generous with virtues.
Sit in the company of the wise and your intelligence will be improved, you will ennoble yourself and your ignorance will be removed from you.
A wise person may [at times also] make a mistake.
He who complains of his troubles to one who is not compassionate is not a wise person.
He who expresses his joy to one who is not his close friend is not a wise person.
He who intends to take his request to one who is not wise (or generous) is not a wise person.
One who unveils the words of the wise benefits from their hidden meanings.
Indeed the speech of a wise person, when it is correct, is a cure and when it is wrong, is a malady.
Obedience is the shield of the people and justice is the shield of governments.
The disgrace after being deposed is equal to the glory of sovereignty.
The humiliation of the man being deposed is equivalent to his evil as a sovereign.
Be just in that which you have been given authority and thank Allah for that which has been granted to you.
Protect your status near your king and be cautious not to be belittled due to [your] negligence in protecting that which elevated you to it.

Direct the people [based] on their practices and religions; let the innocent from among them be safe [from your wrath] and let the suspicious ones be afraid of you, and protect their frontiers and borders.
Make the religion your refuge and justice your sword, [then] you will be safe from every evil and will triumph over every foe.
Be cautious of inequity and tyranny, for verily inequity invites the sword and tyranny leads to expulsion and hastens retribution and revenge.
The most loathsome thing is the tyranny of rulers.
Kingship is politics.
Kingship spoils brotherhood.
Leadership is destruction.
Equity is the embellishment of leadership.
Haughtiness in sovereignty leads to disgrace in deposition.
Sovereignties are the arenas of men.
The instrument of leadership is [patience and] large-heartedness.
The bane of leadership is arrogance.
When you are given a position of authority, [then] act justly.
When the vile become sovereigns, the dignified ones are ruined.
When the depraved gain authority, hope turns into disappointment.
When the wicked become rulers, the honourable are persecuted.
The sovereignty of the vile and inexperienced over nations is the cause of their decline and regression.
Your haughtiness in sovereignty will be [the cause of your] disgrace in deposition.
The stability of nations is through the establishment of the practice of justice.
Love for authority is the primary source of tribulations.
The embellishment of leadership is bestowing favours.
The fall of nations results from the appointment of depraved leaders.
The excellence of leadership is [in] good governance.
Lack of leaders is easier to bear than the leadership of the depraved.
Every nation has its moment.
Nothing ever preserves nations like the exercising of justice in them.
One who oppresses his people helps his enemies.

By the One who split the grain and created human being! If people had not come to me and supporters had not exhausted the argument, and if Allah had not commanded the learned that they should not acquiesce in the excesses of the oppressor and the hunger of the oppressed, I would have cast its rope (i.e. of Caliphate) on its own shoulders and would have given the last one to drink from the cup of the first (i.e. I would have let things remain in their previous state). Then you would have found that in my view, this world of yours is not better than the sneezing of a goat.
The generosity of rulers with booty belonging to the Muslims is [an act of] injustice and betrayal.
A predatory animal that is rapacious and tears it prey apart is better than an unjust and oppressive ruler.
The worst of rulers is one who is feared by the innocent.
One whose rule is oppressive, his regime collapses.
One who is haughty in his rule, his disgrace is greater when he is deposed.
One who becomes vain in his rule exhibits his stupidity.
It is from the right of the shepherd to choose for his flock that which he chooses for himself.
It is part of nobility that you [should] be attentive in fulfilling the rights of your subjects upon you and that you disregard any [of their] offences towards you.
An unjust and oppressive ruler is better than perpetual strife.
There is no oppression more severe than the oppression of a ruler.
How can one be safe from the punishment of Allah when he is quick in making false oaths.

The swearing of a man increases for four [possible reasons]: something shameful that he knows about himself, or as a means of entreating by which he may be deemed truthful, or because of his inability to express himself so he takes oaths as verbiage to connect his speech, or because of an accusation that has been made upon him.
The thing that brings the quickest punishment is a false oath.
Do not habituate yourself to taking oaths, for verily the one who swears excessively is not safe from sin.
You should cling to the lawful, and to treating your family with kindness, and to remembering Allah in all circumstances.
Dreams may [at times] come true.
A good dream is one of the two [forms of] glad-tidings.
The first compensation for the forbearing person from his forbearance is that all the people are [ready to be] his helpers against his enemy.
The forbearing person raises his determination, in that which he has been oppressed, above seeking an evil retribution.

Indeed the best of people is one who is forbearing even when he is strong [enough to exact revenge], is not attached to the pleasures of this world even though he is well-off and is just even though he has power.
The forbearing is one who tolerates [the flaws of] his brothers.
The forbearing is one for whom it is not difficult to act with tolerance.
If you are not forbearing then act forbearing, for verily it is rare for a person who imitates a group not to soon become one among them.
Indeed only he is forbearing who is patient when he is offended and forgives when he is wronged.
Sit in the company of the forbearing and you will increase your forbearance.
Sometimes the forbearing person may get fed up.
A person who is not forbearing may at times dress in the garb of forbearance.
Be forbearing in [times of] anger, very patient [and courageous] in fear, [and] moderate in your request.

He who lacks strength and thus remains quiet, only to take revenge when he gets power, is not forbearing; rather only he is forbearing who forgives when he has power and over all of whose affairs forbearance prevails.
One who endeavours to act with forbearance becomes forbearing.
One who shows forbearance is honoured.
One who adorns himself with forbearance, his recklessness subsides.
One who does not endeavour to act with forbearance does not become forbearing.
Whoever infuriates you by the ugliness of his foolish behaviour towards you, then infuriate him by the beauty of your forbearance towards him.
One who seeks the support of forbearance against you defeats you and acts graciously towards you.
Forbearance is one of the two excellent traits.
Forbearance during intense rage protects [one] from the wrath of the Almighty.
Forbearance puts out the fire of rage and acrimoniousness stokes it.
Be forbearing and you will be honoured.
Be forbearing and you will be respected.
Bear [the actions of others] with patience, otherwise you will never be pleased.
Veil [your] anger with forbearance and ignore misconceptions with understanding.
The strongest of all people is the one who overcomes his anger with his forbearance.
The best forbearance is suppressing anger and exercising self-restraint despite having power [to exact revenge].
The most courageous of people is the one who defeats ignorance with forbearance.
Verily the best of characteristics of men is forbearance.
Delaying punishment is from the perfection of forbearance.
Forbearance is [like] a tribe [as it protects those who belong to it].
Forbearance is the ornament of [one’s] character.
Forbearance is the symbol of excellence.
Forbearance is the cornerstone of [good] leadership.
Forbearance is the fruit of knowledge.
Forbearance is a means of silencing the foolish.
Forbearance is the embellishment of knowledge.
Forbearance is the perfection of intellect.
Forbearance (or wisdom) is light, [and] its essence is the intellect.
Forbearance is the ornament of knowledge and the cause of peace.
Forbearance is the system by which the affairs of a believer are organized.
If in anger there is revenge, then in forbearance there is the reward of the virtuous.
Verily forbearance is only suppression of anger and self-restraint.
The bane of forbearance is humiliation.
When you are forbearing with a foolish person, you sadden him; so increase his sorrow by your forbearance towards him.
When you are forbearing with an ignorant person, you have given him the best reply.
When you hear something hateful that troubles you, then lower your head, taking no notice of it, and it will pass you by.
When forbearance brings about corruption [and defiance in the enemy], forgiveness becomes a weakness.
Through forbearance, supporters increase.
It is through suppression [of anger] that forbearance comes about.
Gulping down the agonies of forbearance extinguishes the fire of anger.
Gulp down the agonies, for indeed I have not seen any drink that is sweeter than this in outcome, nor more tasteful in effect.
Gulp down the pains of forbearance, for indeed it is the cornerstone of wisdom and the fruit of knowledge.
The fruit of forbearance is kindness.
Virtuous forbearance is a sign of abundant knowledge.
The best forbearance is accustoming yourself to act with forbearance.
The cornerstone of knowledge is forbearance.
The alms-tax of forbearance is bearing patiently [with the bad behaviour of the people].
The cause of reverence is forbearance.
Espouse forbearance for verily it is the fruit of knowledge.
Espouse forbearance for indeed it is a pleasing characteristic.
It is when rage and anger prevails that the forbearance of the forbearing is tested.
The strength [required] for forbearance in times of anger is greater than the strength [needed] for vengeance.
Forbearance is sufficient as veneration.
Delaying punishment is from the perfection of forbearance.
The best vizier of knowledge is forbearance.
The dignity of forbearance is the adornment of knowledge.
I found forbearance and tolerance more helpful to me than courageous men.
Do not disgrace yourselves in order to alleviate your anger, and if an ignorant person acts ignorantly towards you then let your forbearance prevail over him.
There is no virtue like forbearance.
There is no supporter like forbearance.
There is no forbearance like feigning inattention [and pretending not to have noticed].
There is no dignity loftier than forbearance.
There is no honour higher than forbearance.
No one shows forbearance towards the foolish except the intelligent.
One who has no forbearance has no knowledge.
The forbearance of a person is evinced from his abundant tolerance, and his nobility [is evinced] from his abundant benefactions.
A Praiser should praise none but his Lord.
Whoever puts praise [for Allah] as the conclusion of a blessing, Allah, the Glorified, makes it the key for more [blessings].
Whoever praises Allah, He makes him free from want.
Try to increase your praiseworthy actions [and traits], for verily disgraceful actions [and traits] are such that very few gain salvation from them.
Be pleased with Muhammad (s) as your guide [and role model] and as the one who will lead you to salvation.
Follow the guidance of your Prophet for it is the truest guidance, and emulate his practices for they are the most exemplary practices.
Be cautious of exceeding the limits with regards to us; say that we are servants of our Lord, and then you may believe anything you wish about our merits.
Indeed we, the household [of the Prophet], are the doors of wisdom, the lights that dispel darkness and the illumination of the nations.

Where are you wandering and where are you coming from and where are you straying to and what are you bewildered by while you have among you the progeny of your Prophet – they who are the guides towards right and speakers of truth?

Where are those who allege that they are firmly grounded in knowledge apart from us, while they lie and transgress against us, and harbour jealousy towards us because Allah, the Glorified, elevated us and lowered them, gave us and deprived them, put us in [His proximity] and expelled them; it is through us that guidance is granted and the blindness [of ignorance] is removed, not though them!
The most virtuous of good deeds is loving us and the most despicable of evil deeds is hating us.

The most fortunate of all people is one who knows our merits, seeks nearness to Allah through us, is sincere in his love for us, acts on that which we have entrusted to him and keeps away from that which we have forbidden, for this person is from us and he will be with us in the Eternal Abode.
The nearest of people to us is one who loyally supports us and has enmity for our enemies.
Indeed, for [the proclamation:] ‘There is none worthy of worship but Allah’ there are some conditions, and verily I and my progeny are from its conditions.
Verily, the beggar is a messenger of Allah, so one who gives to him gives to Allah and one who withholds from him, withholds from Allah, the Glorified.1

text: Verily our affair is difficult and arduous, none can bear it except the servant whose heart Allah has tested for [and filled with] faith, and nothing preserves our words except the faithful hearts and discerning minds.
To us return the ones who exceed the bounds and the ones who lag behind [come forward to] meet up with us.

Verily Allah, the Exalted, made an appraisal of the world and (from it) chose us, and He chose for us followers who would help us, be happy in our happiness and sad in our sadness, and give up their lives and wealth for our sake they are ones who are (considered to be) from us and unto us, and they will be with us in the gardens (of Paradise).

Verily our affair is difficult and arduous, rough and harsh, secret, hidden and veiled, none have access to it except the favoured angel, the appointed prophet or the believer whose heart Allah, the Glorified, has tested for faith.

Indeed here (and he pointed towards his chest) there is great knowledge; if only I could get someone who would bear it. Yes, I do find some who can understand but cannot be relied upon and would use the tools of religion for worldly gain or would dominate the people through the favours of Allah over His servants and through His authority over His friends; or [I find] one who is submissive to those who bear the truth but has no insight or intelligence, misgivings pierce into his heart at the first instance of doubt.
The People of Remembrance (or followers of the Qur’an) are the People of Allah and His favoured ones.

I am the allotter of hellfire, the treasurer of the gardens [of Paradise], the owner of the pond [of Kawthar] and the holder of the Elevations, and there is no Imam from among us, the household [of the Prophet], except that he knows those who are his sincere friends [and followers], and this is the meaning of the words of the Most High: ‘You are only a warner, and there is a guide for every people’2.
I am the brother of the Prophet of Allah, the first to accept Islam, the breaker of the idols, the warrior against the disbelievers and the vanquisher of adversaries.
I am the one who turn this world over on its face, gauges it according to its true value and drives it back on its heels.
I am the leader (ya‘sūb3) of the believers and wealth is the leader of the wicked.

I will be with the Prophet of Allah, the blessings of Allah be upon him, and with me will be my progeny at the pond (so act upon our words and emulate our actions as we will vie at the pond [of Kawthar]), and we will verily drive away our enemies from it and let our close friends drink from it, and whoever takes a drink from it will never be thirsty after that again.
I put the chests of the Arab [warriors] on the ground and broke the backs (or the protruding horns) of the tribes of Rabī‘ah and Mu

text: I am a witness for you [if you follow me] and a plaintiff against you [if you disobey me] on the Day of Judgment.
I am your inviter towards the obedience of your Lord, your mentor to performing your religious obligations and your guide to that which will save you.
My household and I are the [means of] security for the people of earth just as the stars are the [means of] security for the people of the heavens.
I am the representative of the Prophet of Allah among you, and the one who will keep you within the boundaries of your religion, and the one who calls you towards the Garden of the Abode.
Verily I am standing on a manifest proof from my Lord, insight in my religion and certitude in my affair.
Verily I am on the highway of truth and they are surely on the erroneous path of falsehood.
Verily it is for the establishment of the proofs of Allah that I argue and it is in order to support His religion that I struggle and fight.

Indeed I raise myself such that there should be no need that my generosity cannot encompass, nor any ignorance that cannot be encompassed by my forbearance, nor any wrongdoing that my forgiveness cannot encompass, nor should there be a time that is longer than my time [spent in worship and righteous actions].
Whenever I would ask the Prophet of Allah (s), he would give to me and when I was silent and did not ask, he would be the one to initiate [the matter] with me.
The example of my presence among you is only like a lamp in the darkness, he who enters upon it receives its light.

Certainly the Imams are the [only] vicegerents of Allah over His creation and the ones who explain His servants about Him; and none will enter Paradise except the one who recognizes them and is recognized by them and none will enter the hellfire except the one who rejects them and is rejected by them.
Indeed the protectors of the religion of Allah are the only ones who establish the religion, support it, surround it from all sides and protect it for the servants of Allah and safeguard it.

(In remembrance of the Prophet of Allah (s), he said): He conveyed [the message] from his Lord completely, such that nobody remained with any excuse [for not having accepted the message], he counselled his people as a warner and called [them] towards Paradise as a bringer of glad tidings.
Through us you were guided in the darkness, and by us you ascended the peaks [of knowledge and faith], and by way of us did you break through the pitch-black night [into the light of day].

Through us Allah opens and through us Allah seals, through us Allah effaces and confirms whatever He wills, through us Allah removes the time of difficulty [or intense thirst and drought] and through us Allah sends down rain; so let not the Deceiver deceive you concerning Allah.

Mingle with the people through that which they recognize and leave them in that which they reject, and do not burden them [by compelling them] to follow yourselves and us, for indeed our affair is difficult and arduous.

He (‘a) said about the Prophet of Allah (s): He left this world hungry but entered the next world in soundness. He did not lay one brick upon another [to make a house for himself] until he passed away and responded to the caller of his Lord.
The caller is calling and the guardian is watching over you, so respond to the caller and follow the guardian.
Ask me [about what you need to know] before you lose me, for verily I am more aware of the ways of the heavens than you are of the ways of the earth.

Ask me before you lose me, for by Allah, there is no verse in the Qur’an but that I know about whom it was revealed and where it was revealed, in the plains or on the mountains, and indeed my Lord has gifted me with an intelligent heart and an eloquent tongue.

Remembering the Prophet of Allah (s), he (‘a) said: His practice was moderation, his action was right guidance, his speech was distinguishing [of truth from falsehood], his judgment was just, his words were articulate and his silence was the most eloquent speech.
Attach yourselves to the one who is between you and Allah, [and] you will be felicitous.
Establish your bond with the one who is between you and Allah, [and] you will be felicitous in your final place of return [in the Hereafter].

Remembering the Prophet of Allah (s) he said: [He was] a physician who moved about with his remedies, having readied his salves and warmed his instruments. He used these whenever needed for curing blind hearts, deaf ears and dumb tongues. He would take his cures to the places of negligence and sites of perplexity.

You should love of the progeny of your Prophet, for this is the right of Allah over you and this will obligate your right upon Allah. Do you not see that Allah has said ‘Say, I do not ask you any reward for it except love of (my) near relatives.’
You must obey your Imams, for they are witnesses over you today and intercessors for you with Allah tomorrow.
It is the duty of the Imam to teach the people who follow him about the boundaries of Islam and Imān (faith).

The [leader and] guide must be truthful to his followers and must employ his intellect; and he must be from those who are inclined to the Hereafter, for it is from there that he came forth and to it will be his return.
The riser has risen, the dazzler has dazzled, the apparent has appeared and the crooked has been straightened.4

text: He said while remembering the Messenger of Allah (s): He belittled this world, took it lightly and treated it with disdain; he knew that Allah willed to keep it away from him while He bestowed it to others as a trial.
Whenever I asked the Messenger of Allah (s), he would give to me and when I held back, he would be the one to initiate [the matter] with me.
For our hatred there are waves of wrath from Allah, the Glorified.

I have patched this shirt of mine so much that I am now ashamed of [taking it again to] the tailor. Someone asked me: Will you not discard it? I replied: Get away from me! Only at dawn do people speak highly of the [arduous] night journey.
This world will incline towards us after having been refractory just like the wild camel inclines towards its young.
I am not, nor have I ever been, intimidated by battle or frightened of being struck [by swords].
If the veils were removed, my certitude would not increase.5
flag_note: Contains a stray character/number at the end of the sentence.

text: If my feet were to rest firmly on these slippery areas, I would surely change [many] things.
If we had done as you did, no pillar of the religion would be left standing and no plant of faith would grow.

If I wished to inform every man from among you of where he has come from and where he is going to and about all his affairs, I would do so, but I fear that you will take me and abandon the Messenger of Allah, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him. However, I will convey it to the selected ones who are safe from that [fear]. By the One who sent him with truth and chose him above the creation, I do not speak save the truth. He (the Prophet) has informed me about all this and about the destruction of those who are destroyed and the salvation of those who are saved (and the consequences of this matter [of the caliphate]). He left nothing that I would encounter except that he put it into my ear and informed me about it.
We have a right [to it] if it is given to us, otherwise we ride on the hinds of camels6 even if the night journey is long.
flag_note: Contains a stray footnote reference number.

text: We have the right of obedience and love over the people, and for them [for this] there is a goodly reward from Allah, the Glorified.
Whoever clings to us will join us.
Whoever turns away from us will be annihilated.
One who follows our commandments advances.
One who boards other than our ship, drowns.

They (i.e. the Imams) are the trustees of the secrets of the Messenger of Allah (s), the protectors of his mission, the container of his knowledge, the sanctuary of his wisdom, the caverns of his books and the mountains of his religion.
They are the gems of faith and the treasures of the Most Merciful. When they speak, they are truthful and when they remain silent, they are not surpassed.
They are the treasures of faith and the sources of virtue; when they judge, they do justice and when they debate, they overcome.
They are the foundation of religion and the pillar of certitude; to them return those who have exceeded the limits and those who are behind [come forward to] join them.
They are the lamps in the darkness, the springs of wisdom, the sources of knowledge and the loci of forbearance.

They are the life of knowledge and the death of ignorance. Their forbearance (or wisdom) is conveyed to you from their knowledge, their silence from their speech (and their apparent from their hidden); they do not go against the truth (or the religion) nor do they differ in it, for it is among them as a silent speech and a truthful witness.
Do not stray from the truth and its people, for verily whoever opts [to follow] other than us, the household [of the Prophet], perishes and loses in [both] this world and the Hereafter.

The world is never devoid of an establisher of the proof of Allah, either [as an] apparent and known [person] or [as a] hidden and unknown [person], so that the proof of Allah and His message does not become void.

No one from this nation can be compared to the progeny of Muhammad, peace and blessings of Allah be upon him, and no one who has benefitted from their blessings (i.e. the blessings of their knowledge and wisdom) will ever be equal to them.

People! There is no proof of Allah, the Glorified, on His earth greater than our Prophet, Muhammad (s), nor is there any wisdom more manifest than His book, the Glorious Qur’an and Allah, the Exalted, has not praised anyone from among you except he who holds fast to his rope and follows His prophet; and only he perishes, who perishes when he disobeys Him, goes against His commands and follows his vain desires. This is why the Almighty says ‘... let those who disobey His order beware lest an ordeal should afflict them or a painful chastisement befall them.’7
flag_note: The text contains a stray citation number '7' at the end of the quotation.

text: The one who looks with the insight of the wise sees his path of guidance (or goal) and knows its valleys and its peaks.
We are the callers to truth, the leaders of creation and the speakers of truth, he who obeys us acquires [success] and he who disobeys us is destroyed.
By Allah! I have never hidden a single word nor have I ever spoken a lie.
By Allah! I do not hate the sudden coming of death to me, nor is it an event that I reject. I am but like a traveller who has come to his destination or a seeker who finds what he is looking for.

By Allah! If I were to spend a sleepless night on the thorns of al-Sa‘dān8 or be driven shackled in chains as a prisoner, it would be more acceptable to me than meeting Allah and His Prophet as an oppressor over any [of His] servants, or a usurper of any worldly possessions. And how can I oppress for the sake of the body which is fast moving towards destruction and is going to spend a long time [buried] in the earth?
flag_note: The text contains a stray citation number '8' attached to a word.

text: The devout companions of the Messenger of Allah (s) know that I never disobeyed Allah, the Glorified, or His Prophet for even a moment; and I supported him in situations where the valiant ones retreated and when the feet were slow in moving forward with courage – Allah honoured me with [all] this. I spared no effort in his obedience, may the blessings of Allah be upon him, and I fought his enemies with all my might, and I put my life on the line in order to protect him, and he divulged to me from his knowledge that which he did not divulge to anyone other than me.

Knowledge has led them to real understanding and they have acquired the spirit of conviction. They take easy what the easygoing regard as hard. They are comfortable with that which the ignorant are repelled by. They live in this world with their bodies but their spirits are in the higher realm. They are the vicegerents of Allah on His earth and the callers to His religion. Ah, ah! How I yearn to see them.

They are the supports of Islam and those entrusted with its protection. Through them the truth is restored in its rightful place and falsehood is removed from its position with its tongue is severed from its root. They have understood religion through reflection and contemplation, not by mere hearsay and [blind following of] what is narrated.
Verily we are the masters of speech; in us its offshoots (or veins) are fixed and its branches hang over us.
The chain of delusion will never be severed until the rising of the [Imam of the] avenger of the age.
We are the door of ‘Ḥiṭṭah’ which is the door of peace; one who enters it is safe and secure, whereas one who turns away from it is destroyed.
We are the middle cushion which is joined by those who remain behind and to which those who have exceeded the limits return.
We are the trustees of Allah over His servants and the establishers of truth in His lands. Through us the friend [of Allah] is saved and by us the enemy is destroyed.

We are the [family] tree of Prophethood, the station of revelation, the ones upon whom angels descend, the fountains of wisdom and the sources of knowledge. Our helpers and lovers await mercy while our enemies and haters await wrath.

We are the nearest ones [to the Prophet (s)], the companions, the custodians [of the treasures of Paradise] and the doors [of knowledge and wisdom]; and houses are not entered but through their doors, and whoever enters them without going through their doors is [considered] a thief and is not spared punishment.
Far be it! If there was no command of piety, I would have been the most cunning of all the Arabs.
I have never rejected Allah from the time that I came to know Him.
I have never doubted in the truth since the time it was shown to me.
I have never lied nor have I been accused of lying.
I have never strayed [from the right path] nor has anyone gone astray because of me.

No verse [of the Qur’an] was revealed but that I knew the occasion of its revelation and where it was revealed, [whether] in daytime or night, on a mountain or a plain; and my Lord has gifted me with an intelligent heart and an eloquent tongue.
We have established the pillar of truth and vanquished the forces of falsehood.
Foolishness is occupying oneself with the superfluous and accompanying the ignorant.
Foolishness is an ailment which cannot be remedied and a sickness that cannot be cured.
The worst indigence is foolishness.
The most harmful thing is foolishness.
The height of foolishness is being beguiled [by the pleasures of this world].
The greatest foolishness is exaggeration in praise and censure.
The greatest foolishness is being conceited in [the state of] poverty.
Foolishness is a disgrace.
Foolishness is the most harmful companion.
Foolishness is the worst ailment.
Foolishness leads to superfluity.
Foolishness is from the fruits of ignorance.
Foolishness makes one a stranger in his own hometown.
How bad an ailment foolishness is!
The poverty of foolishness is not alleviated by [material] wealth.
Being conceited in poverty is the height of foolishness.
Establishing brotherhood with the vicious is from the greatest [acts of] foolishness.
Being audacious in front of the king is an act of foolishness.
From the signs of foolishness are: being audacious without any means and boasting without [possessing] any nobility.
With foolishness, what is sought is not achieved.
There is no ailment worse than foolishness.
There is no poverty more severe than foolishness.
Foolishness is wretchedness.
The fool is a stranger in his [own] hometown, [and is] humiliated among his near ones.
A fool does not improve by abasement and he is does not separate from fault and loss.
flag_note: contains grammatical error 'he is does not'

text: Be wary of the fool for verily, being amicable with him will bring you hardship (or exhaust you), agreeing with him will destroy you, disagreeing with him will cause you suffering and keeping his company will be [like] a curse upon you.
The most foolish of all people is the one who thinks that he is the most intelligent of all people.
The most foolish of all people is the one who prevents good deeds and [then] seeks gratitude, and does evil and [then] expects the reward for [doing] good.
The most foolish of all people is the one who censures others for a vice while he [himself] performs it.
The fool does not improve by being disgraced.
The remoteness of a fool is better than his nearness and his silence is better than his speech.
The foolishness of a person is recognized by [his] cheerfulness in times of blessing and increased abjectness in times of tribulation.
The foolishness of a person is recognized in three things: in his talking about that which does not concern him, [in] his answering that which he was not asked and his recklessness in [his] affairs.
Cutting off [ties with] the fool is judiciousness.
Be cautious of the fool when you are in his company, of the vicious when you associate with him and of the oppressor when you deal with him.
For the fool there is an oath with every statement.1
flag_note: contains a stray numerical character at the end of the sentence

text: Be careful not to love the fool, for he will surely harm you while he thinks that he is benefitting you and will annoy you while he thinks that he is pleasing you.
Keeping silent is the best response for a fool.
Increased fickleness is from the signs of a fool.
Putting up with a fool is a torment for the soul.
Never show respect to a fool, even if he is [apparently] great.
Tolerance is proof of intelligence and a symbol of excellence.
Tolerance is the ornament of companionship.
Tolerance is the embellishment of politics [and leadership].
Tolerance dignifies one’s status.
Tolerance is a beautiful quality.
Tolerating meanness (or annoyance) is from nobility of character.
By bearing the burden of provision (for the people), praises increase.
Through increased tolerance, one’s merit (or intelligence) increases.
Through tolerance and forbearance, people become your helpers and supporters.
The forbearing one is recognized by his increased tolerance.
Be tolerant, [and] your status will become lofty.
Adopt tolerance, for verily it is [a means of] concealing faults.
One whose tolerance increases becomes noble.
One who does not bear the burden of providing for the people has prepared his power for its transference.
flag_note: The phrasing 'prepared his power for its transference' is nonsensical and likely a mistranslation or corrupted text.

text: It is part of honour to tolerate the wrongdoings of [one’s] brothers.
Tolerate that which comes your way, for indeed tolerance is a [means of] concealing faults and verily the wise one is half [the time] tolerant and half [the time] feigning negligence.
Continually bearing the liabilities [of others] causes loftiness [of character].
It is to the extent of one’s vehemence that one is protective of his honour.
Allah! Allah! I warn you servants of Allah, against feeling proud of your bigotry and boasting over your ignorance, for indeed these are the fertilizers of enmity and the bellows of Satan.
There is no vehemence in one who has no sense of honour.
Fitness of the body is [in] abstinence from [harmful] foods.
One who cannot patiently bear the agony of abstinence [from food], his sickness will be prolonged.
Verily the needs of the people that are addressed to you are a blessing from Allah upon you, so take advantage of them and do not be weary of them, lest they should turn into [divine] wrath.
Do not delay granting the needy to tomorrow, for you do not know what will happen to you and to him tomorrow.

You must seek the fulfilment of your needs through people of honourable dispositions and origins, you will be successful [in getting what you need] with them, without any delay or any sense of obligation.
You must seek your needs from those who are honourable and of good origins, for they are more likely to fulfil them [quickly and without obligation] and they are purer in your eyes.

I am amazed at the person who is approached by his Muslim brother in need and refuses to fulfil it, not deeming himself worthy of [doing] good; so assume that he does not desire any reward nor does he fear any punishment. Do they lack interest in [acquiring] noble traits?
Not having your needs fulfilled is better than seeking them from those who are not worthy.
Being generous with power [and fulfilling the needs of the people with it] is the alms-tax of power.
Expediting the release [of the needy from his need] is [a means of] success.

The fulfilling of needs is not made righteous except by three things: by considering it to be small such that it becomes great, by hiding it such that it is made apparent [by Allah] and by expediting it such that it becomes felicitous.
Everyone who has been given time [to do good before his death] gives excuses for postponement [of good deeds].
Turning away the needy is the cause of diminishment of affluence.
Express your needs to whomever you wish and (you will) become his captive.
When you express your needs to someone, you abase yourself before him.
One who seeks his needs from you, his obedience to you will be to the extent of his need from you.

When someone turns to you with his needs, it becomes obligatory upon you to help him. How are you? is driving towards death, whose state of health can be changed to sickness at any moment and who can be approached [by death] from his place of safety?!
flag_note: The text contains a nonsensical transition and a sudden shift in topic mid-sentence.

text: It is possible for the one who is perplexed and bewildered to be excused.
Subtlety in [seeking] recourse is the most advantageous of all ways.
For everything there is recourse.
One who neglects his recourse (or natural disposition) is made to rise [towards it] by tribulations.
The living one is never satisfied [and always seeks more].
The fruit of long life is illness and senility.
The end of [this] life is death.
How close is life to death!
How near is the living one to the dead because he will soon join him!
How far is the dead one from the living by his separation from him!
Being ashamed in front of Allah, the Glorified, protects [one] from the punishment of hell.
The most modest among you are the most forbearing among you.
The best of religious attires is modesty.
The greatest modesty is your being ashamed in front of Allah.
The best modesty is your being ashamed of yourself [in front of Allah].
Verily modesty and chastity are from the characteristics of faith, and they are the traits of the free and the qualities of the virtuous.
Modesty is beautiful.
Modesty is preventive.
Shame prevents livelihood.1
flag_note: Contains stray character/footnote marker at the end of the text.

text: Modesty is the key to (every) good.
Shame is accompanied by deprivation.
Modesty is the lowering of one’s gaze.
Modesty is the perfection of honour.
Modesty is the partner of chastity.
Modesty is a beautiful quality.
Modesty is a pleasing characteristic.
Modesty is the perfection of honour and the best of traits.
Modesty prevents one from ugly actions.
Being ashamed in front of Allah effaces many of the sins [that one has committed].
Dress yourself with modesty, wear the armour of loyalty, safeguard brotherhood and reduce your conversations with women, [if you do all this] your eminence will become complete.
The fruit of modesty is chastity.

Three things that are not to be ashamed of [are]: for a person to serve his guest, and for him to stand up from his place for his father or his teacher, and [for him] to seek the right even if it is little.
The shame of person feels from himself is the fruit of [his] faith.

That which is not appropriate for you to do in the open should not be done by you in private.
The best partner of generosity is modesty.

Do not relate that which you have no knowledge about.
Never transmit information except from a reliable person otherwise you will become a liar, and if you transmit from other than him then surely telling lies is [a cause of] disgrace and dishonour.
Do not hasten to the people with that which they dislike so that they [begin to] speak about you that which they do not know.

Analyze the information when you hear it with the analysis of understanding (i.e. in order to understand it), not the analysis of narration (i.e. in order to narrate it to others), for indeed the narrators of information are many but those who consider it carefully are few.

Accompany [people] so that you may gauge [their true nature].

Beware of [engaging in] deception, for verily deception is from the qualities of the vile.

Beat your servant when he disobeys Allah but forgive him when he disobeys you.

One whose enemy is Allah, the Glorified, his proof is refuted and he is punished in this world and in his Hereafter.

Put cotton in your inkpot, keep the nib of your pen long, leave space between your lines and keep the letters close to each other, for this makes the writing more beautiful.

The imbuement of ideas is through deliberation.
The daring risk-taker charges towards danger.
Making many mistakes points towards excessive ignorance.
Sincerity is in grave danger, until it is seen what it concludes with.
Be sincere and you will attain [success].
Let your action, your knowledge, your love, your hatred, your taking, your leaving, your speech and your silence [all] be [sincerely] for the sake of Allah.

How strange it is that the succession [to the Prophet] is [decided] by companionship [only] and not by companionship and kinship.

You should be zealous for praiseworthy qualities like protecting the [rights of the] neighbour, fulfilling the sureties, obedience to virtue and opposition to arrogance; and beautify yourselves with excellent traits.
Choose for yourself the best from every character [trait], for indeed virtue is a habit.
Good character is [an embellishment] for the soul and good appearance is [a beautification] for the body.
Adopting a good character is the best [means of following the] religion.
Good character is the best companion and self-conceit is a hidden ailment.
Good character is from the best allotment and the most virtuous of qualities.
Good character is one of the two bounties [of Allah].
Good character is proof of an honourable ancestry.
Good character increases sustenance and makes companions feel at ease.
Good character is the cornerstone of all virtuous acts.
Good character brings about adoration and strengthens love.
The best character is the one that is furthest from obstinacy.
The best of qualities is the most agreeable of them.
The best of attributes is kindness.
The best of all qualities is truthfulness in speech and noble actions.
The foundation of belief is [adopting a] good character and adorning oneself with the truth.

I had, in the past, a brother-in-faith and his view of the world as something insignificant made him great in my eyes. He was above being controlled by the needs of his appetency and thus he never craved for what he could not get nor would he ask for more of what he got. He was silent most of the time but when he spoke, he silenced the other speakers and quenched the thirst [for answers] of questioners. He was [apparently] weak and feeble but at the time of battle he was like the lion of the forest or the serpent of the valley. He would not put forth an argument unless it was decisive. He would not accuse anyone in an excusable matter until he had heard his excuse. He would not mention any suffering except after recovering from it. He would do as he says and not say that which he does not do [himself]. Even when (or if) he could be exceeded in speaking, he could not be excelled in silence. He was more eager to listen than he was to speak. When two things came before him, he would see which of the two was closer to vain desire and would oppose it. You should [all] adopt these qualities, thus acquire them and compete with each other in them. And if you cannot acquire them, you should know that acquiring a little is better than giving up plenty.
Nothing gets constricted with good character.
One whose character is noble, his sustenance is increased.
One whose qualities are good, his companionship is pleasant.
One whose character is good, his ways become easy.
One whose character is good, more people adore him and feel at ease with him.
Allah, the Glorified, does not give a servant anything from the good of this world or the Hereafter but because of his good character and his good intention.
The best distinction is good character.
The best trait is [having a] good character.

He (‘a) said about the one whom he censured: If he falls sick he regrets having abandoned the work and if he is healthy, he feels secure and delays the work. When he is called to cultivate for this world, he works and when he is called to cultivate for the Hereafter, he is lazy. If he becomes wealthy, he turns arrogant and falls into vice and if he becomes poor, he despairs and becomes weak. If a favour is done to him, he is ungrateful and if he does a favour, he lengthens it and makes it seem like [a great favour and] an obligation. If an evil deed presents itself to him, he commits it with the excuse of seeking repentance [for it later] but when he decides to repent, he delays it and persists in sinning. If he experiences wellbeing, he assumes that he has repented. If he is distressed, he thinks [ill of Allah] and doubts [in Him]. If he falls ill he devotes himself and turns repentantly [to Allah] but if he regains his health, he forgets and returns [to his evil ways] and becomes emboldened in his injustice towards the servants [of Allah]. Every creation is moving towards that which it has no knowledge of.
The cause of immorality is seclusion.
Remaining in seclusion (when it is required to safeguard faith) is the habit of the righteous.
Abandoning the drinking of wine is [commanded as] a protection for the mind.

Five [types of people] are worthy of being humiliated: The one who interferes between two people when they have not involved him in their affair, the one who issues commands to the owner of the house [while] in his house, the one who approaches a dining table when he has not been invited to do so, the one who continues talking when nobody is listening and the one who sits in the place where he has no right to sit.
Five qualities are detested from five [people]: Excessive licentiousness from scholars, greed from sages, stinginess from the wealthy, shamelessness from women and from the elders, adultery.

Fear [of Allah] is the imprisonment of the self from sins and its impediment from vices.
